scope: sha256 of the 545 protected M1d paths as they must appear in the live working tree

supersedes.reason: The semantic closure guard, verify_semantic_closure in src/drift/domain/semantic_attestation.py, missed aliased and indirect dynamic imports (#106 review finding F2): an aliased import_module, pkgutil.resolve_name, functools.partial over a loader, and importlib.util.find_spec followed by exec_module all reached an undeclared drift module while the closure proof stayed green. The guard now fails closed on every name that denotes the import machinery unless it can bind that use to an exact module. That edit changed the bytes of the one path listed in superseded_paths, so the v5 pin for that path no longer describes the live working tree. The declared closures and their resolved module sets are unchanged; because the module is declared in both M1d closures, the m1d-source-validation-v1 and m1d-evidence-v1 attestation values move with its bytes. v5 still describes commit 200bfeb exactly and stays preserved; it is superseded only as the working-tree source freeze. No historical fixture, replay baseline or archive pin changes: pinned replay still recomputes each generation's original identity from its own archived source.

reconstruction: sha256 == the v5 inventory's sha256 map, itself re-derived from v4 and v3, with exactly the keys in superseded_paths replaced by their current_sha256. Each historical_sha256 is the v5 pin of that path, which is its sha256 at supersedes.commit; each current_sha256 is the sha256 of that path in the working tree. A superseded path must be pinned by v5 and an added path must be absent from it. Enforced at load time by tests/_pinned_m1d.py.
